zh.before: 可以查到的是，直到1990年，用的是一个一百二十毫秒的标准，而一百毫秒此后成了国际田联的标准，一些后来的记述把它出现在规则里的时间定在1991年前后。但找不到任何一份数字化的国际田联代表大会记录或者技术委员会决议，既说采用零点一零零秒，又指认一个具体的实验作为它的证据基础。

en.before: What can be established is that a 120-millisecond standard was used until 1990, and that 100 milliseconds subsequently became the IAAF standard. Some later accounts date its appearance in the rules to around 1991. But no digitized IAAF Congress record or Technical Committee resolution has been located that both adopts 0.100 seconds and identifies a specific experiment as its evidential basis.
en.after: Pain and Hibbs's 2007 review says that the earlier criterion was 120 milliseconds until 1990, followed by 100 milliseconds. Other later accounts place the change around 1991. This essay has not located an original IAAF Congress record or Technical Committee resolution that both first adopts 0.100 seconds and identifies a specific experimental basis. Retrospective accounts provide a lead, not the decision itself.

zh.before: 而这个空缺在这里有一个特别的意味。一个数字，如果它真的是从一个确立它的实验来的，那么它还带着一个可以追溯的经验根据。可是这个数字，连它是从哪一篇论文，哪一次会议来的都查不到，而它偏偏被当作一个科学确立的常数在使用。它的权威，超过了它的出身所能支撑的。
zh.after: 这个空缺仍然值得追问。规则在现场可以精确执行，支撑它的知识却应当允许别人核对。找不到首次采用的完整记录，不等于证明当年没有依据；它意味着，今天不能只把“规则就是这样”当作“这个生理常数已经被最终证明”的替代。规则的权威与知识的根据，需要分别交代。

en.before: Here that gap has a particular significance. If a number truly comes from an experiment that established it, it retains an empirical basis that can be traced. Yet the paper or meeting from which this number originated cannot even be located, while the number is used as if it were a scientifically established constant. Its authority exceeds what its provenance can support.
en.after: The gap still matters. A rule can operate precisely on the field while its evidential basis remains open to scrutiny. Not finding a complete adoption record does not prove that no grounds existed at the time. It means that “this is the rule” cannot substitute for “this physiological constant has been conclusively established.” Institutional authority and evidential justification require separate accounts.

zh.before: 这是一个特别重要的档案点，值得把它的含义说透。这个构，有它自己委托产生的，建议一个更低限制的证据，却保留了现有的法律标准。这说明零点一零零秒不是一个被科学锁定的常数，如果它是，那么当科学建议改的时候它就该改。它是一个被机构选择保留的定义。构面对它自己的证据，选择了不动那条线。
zh.after: 这个档案点很重要：机构委托的研究建议降低阈值，而规则继续保留原数。它至少说明，研究建议和规则修订并不会自动同步。七名运动员的研究并不是科学的最终表决，但它提出的问题，值得机构回应。零点一零零秒是一条可执行的制度标准，不该只凭它仍在规则里，就被说成已经锁定的生理常数。

en.before: This is a particularly important archival point, and its implications deserve to be made explicit. The construct possessed evidence it had commissioned itself recommending a lower limit, yet retained the existing legal standard. That shows that 0.100 seconds is not a constant locked in place by science. If it were, it should change when science recommended change. It is a definition that an institution has chosen to retain. Confronted with its own evidence, the construct chose not to move the line.
en.after: This is an important documentary contrast: commissioned research recommended a lower threshold, while the rule retained the existing number. At minimum, research recommendations and rule revisions do not move automatically together. A seven-athlete study is not science's final vote, but its questions deserve an institutional response. The continued existence of an operational standard does not make it a conclusively established physiological constant.

findings.kind: source-level; synchronize eight languages if accepted
findings.reason: 假设遇一项研究不自动已推翻；保程序区别。

zh.before: 这件事本身就证明了假设和定义的区别。如果零点一零零秒还是一个假设，那么面对建议它下调的证据，它应该被修正。它没有被修正，恰恰说明它已经不是假设了，它是定义。而定义不因为证据而改变，它只因为机构的决定而改变，而这个机构决定不改。
zh.after: 这让假设与规则的区别更清楚。生理假设需要接受新证据，也需要比较不同研究的测量方法；一项建议本身不是自动完成的反证。规则则还要经过正式修订才能改变。两者不是互不相干，而是更新的方式不同：研究提出重新审查的理由，机构需要说明为什么改、为什么暂时不改。

en.before: This fact itself demonstrates the distinction between hypothesis and definition. If 0.100 seconds were still a hypothesis, evidence recommending a reduction should have revised it. That it was not revised shows precisely that it was no longer a hypothesis: it was a definition. A definition changes not through evidence alone but through an institutional decision, and the institution decided not to change it.
en.after: This clarifies the distinction between a hypothesis and a rule. A physiological hypothesis must face new evidence and comparisons between measurement methods; one recommendation is not an automatic refutation. A rule also needs formal revision before it changes. The two are connected but updated differently: research gives reasons for reconsideration, and the institution should explain why it changes the rule or retains it for now.

zh.before: 要公道地说，构不改也未必全无道理。频繁改动一个基础的判罚标准，本身有代价，它会让不同年代的成绩更难比较，会让运动员和裁判无所适从，会引入新的争议。所以保留一个虽然有瑕疵，但已经运行多年的标准，有它稳定性上的考虑。但这恰恰印证了这一篇的论点:构保留零点一零零秒，依据的是稳定性，可执行性，行政上的方便，而不是这个数字在生理上正确。它保留它，不是因为它是对的，是因为改它麻烦。而一个因为改起来麻烦所以被保留的数字，已经彻底不是一个生理常数了，它是一个行政上的定义，它的存续理由和人能多快反应，已经没有关系。
zh.after: 公道地说，保留标准可能有理由。改动基础判罚线有过渡成本，也要评估研究结果能否适用于认证设备、怎样区分预判与真实反应，以及不同误判的风险。但这些是需要说明和检验的理由，不是本篇已经取得的完整决策记录。我们不能因为那条线没改，就断言只是嫌麻烦；也不能因为它仍有效，就不再追问它与人的真实反应能力是否相称。

en.before: To be fair, refusing change is not necessarily without reason. Repeatedly altering a basic adjudicative standard has costs of its own. It makes performances across eras harder to compare, leaves athletes and officials uncertain, and introduces new disputes. Retaining a flawed standard that has operated for years thus has an argument from stability. But this confirms the essay's point: the grounds for retaining 0.100 seconds are stability, enforceability and administrative convenience, rather than the number's physiological correctness. It is retained not because it is right, but because changing it is troublesome. A number preserved because revision is troublesome has ceased altogether to be a physiological constant. It is an administrative definition, whose reason for survival is no longer connected to how fast people can react.
en.after: To be fair, retaining a standard may have reasons. Changing a basic adjudicative threshold has transition costs. It also requires assessing whether study results transfer to certified equipment, how anticipation is distinguished from genuine response, and the risks of different errors. These are reasons to explain and test, not a complete decision record recovered here. An unchanged line does not prove mere administrative convenience, just as a valid rule does not end questions about its fit with human reaction.

zh.before: 有人可能会说，构保留零点一零零秒，也许是因为科学还没有定论，那个真正的人类极限还不清楚。这个辩护本身，恰恰暴露了另一件事:那个生理的下限，根本不是一个稳定的常数。

en.before: One might say that the construct retains 0.100 seconds because the science is not yet settled and the true human limit remains unclear. That defence itself exposes something else: the physiological lower limit is not a stable constant at all.
en.after: Perhaps the line is retained partly because the research remains unsettled. That possibility deserves attention. The literature does not supply an agreed lower limit that can be transferred to every competition device regardless of stimulus conditions, response definitions and detection methods. Not having such a number is not proof that a physiological lower bound can never exist.

zh.before: 所以那个被写成定义的零点一零零秒，它背后本应对应的那个生理常数，并不存在一个公认的值。构把一个连科学都没有收敛的东西，冻结成了一个精确到毫秒的定义。定义的精确，和它背后那个生理事实的不确定，形成了一个巨大的反差。这又是精确掩盖无据，而且是一个新的形态:一个精确的阈值，掩盖了它背后那个从来没有被稳定确立的常数。
zh.after: 所以，零点一零零秒背后，并没有一个脱离测量方法便获得普遍认同的生理值。比赛需要精确到毫秒的操作线，相关知识却仍带着条件。两者之间有真实的反差。需要警惕的，不是精确本身，而是把规则的精确，讲成它背后所有生理问题都已经解决。

en.before: Behind the 0.100 seconds written into the definition, then, the physiological constant to which it is supposed to correspond has no agreed value. The construct has frozen something on which science has not converged into a definition precise to the millisecond. The definition's precision stands in enormous contrast to the uncertainty of the physiological fact behind it. Once again, precision conceals a lack of foundation, now in a new form: an exact threshold conceals a constant that has never been stably established.
en.after: Behind 0.100 seconds there is no physiological value universally agreed independently of the measurement method. Competition needs an operational line precise to milliseconds, while the relevant knowledge remains conditional. That is a genuine contrast. The danger is not precision itself, but presenting precision in a rule as proof that all the physiological questions behind it have been settled.

zh.before: 这个反差还有一层，比前面几篇更进一步。第七篇的计分系数，第十二篇的四十毫米，第十四篇的睾酮阈值，那些精确的线背后，是一个没有被推导出来的数，它们的问题是缺一个推导。这里的问题更深:零点一零零秒背后要对应的那个东西，那个人类反应的生理下限，不只是没被推导出来，而是根本不存在一个确定的值可供推导。科学在这个问题上不是还差一步就收敛，而是朝着相反的方向发散，有人说更快，有人说更慢。所以这条线不只是缺一个推导，它是被划在一片本身就没有确定答案的地方，然后被当成了那个确定的答案。
zh.after: 这与前几篇的线还有一层不同。这里不只是问一个数怎样推导，还要问究竟把什么叫作反应：神经活动的开始、力量达到阈值，还是可见动作的开始？统计上怎样判断预判，又是另一个问题。若把这些问题压成同一个“人类极限”，不同结果便容易被误读成对一个常数的简单争执。规则仍需选一条线，但应说清它对应的测量条件与误判风险，而不是假装所有方法都已经给出同一个答案。

en.before: There is another layer to this contrast, taking us beyond the earlier essays. The scoring coefficients in Essay 7, the 40 millimetres in Essay 12 and the testosterone threshold in Essay 14 were precise lines backed by numbers that had not been derived. Their problem was a missing derivation. Here the problem goes deeper. What 0.100 seconds is supposed to correspond to, the physiological lower limit of human reaction, has not merely gone underived. There is no definite value available to derive. Science is not one step short of convergence; it is diverging in opposite directions, some arguing faster, others slower. The line therefore lacks more than a derivation. It has been drawn in a domain that itself has no definite answer, and then treated as that definite answer.
en.after: There is another layer here. The question is not only how to derive a number, but what counts as the response: the onset of neural activity, force reaching a threshold, or visible movement. A statistical judgment about anticipation is another task again. Compressing them into one “human limit” makes different findings look like a simple quarrel over one constant. Rules still need a line, but should explain its measurement conditions and error risks rather than imply that every method has supplied the same answer.

en.before: To use Bolt's 2011 case as evidence that a genuine sub-100-millisecond response was prohibited is to conflate two different questions. Bolt's recorded movement preceded the gun. Allen in 2022, not Bolt in 2011, is the characteristic example of a measured positive reaction time falling just below 100 milliseconds and being rejected by the law of the event.
en.after: Bolt's pre-gun movement in 2011 therefore cannot demonstrate the prohibition of a genuine auditory response below 100 milliseconds. Allen's 2022 reading raises a different question: how does a positive value just below the warning threshold combine with other information to support an on-field decision? The cases are not the same.

zh.before: 艾伦这个立场的分寸很值得注意，因为它恰好落在这一篇要区分的那条线上。他没有争辩说，零点零九九在规则下不算抢跑，那样他就是在争论规则的字面意思，而规则的字面意思是清楚的，零点零九九确实低于零点一零零。他争的是另一件事，他说这条规则本身，连同支撑它的那个生理假设和那套测量设备，应该被重新审视。也就是说，他不是在说裁判用错了定义，他是在说这个定义本身可能是错的。而这恰恰是一个定义最难被撼动的地方，因为定义在自己的框架内永远是对的，零点零九九低于零点一零零，这在定义内无可争辩，要质疑它，只能从定义之外，质疑这个定义该不该是这个样子。
zh.after: 艾伦的主张可以放在这个区分上理解。他承认现场按规则作出了判罚，同时要求重新审视阈值、设备和测量不确定性。零点零九九小于零点一零零，这是算术；它是否足以与其他信息一起支持那次抢跑认定，则是个案适用问题；阈值应该放在哪里，又是规则设计问题。不能把这三层合并，也不必把规则说成在自己的框架里永远正确，才能追问规则之外的理由。

en.before: The care in Allen's position deserves attention, because it falls exactly on the distinction this essay seeks to draw. He did not argue that 0.099 was not a false start under the rules. That would have been an argument about their literal meaning, which is clear: 0.099 is indeed below 0.100. His challenge was different. The rule itself, together with its supporting physiological hypothesis and measurement equipment, should be re-examined. In other words, he was not saying that the officials had misapplied the definition. He was saying that the definition itself might be wrong. That is precisely where a definition is hardest to unsettle, because within its own framework it is always right. Within the definition, 0.099 being less than 0.100 is indisputable. To challenge it, one must step outside and ask whether the definition ought to take this form at all.
en.after: Allen's position can be understood through this distinction. He accepted that officials had ruled under the existing rules while calling for reconsideration of the threshold, equipment and measurement uncertainty. That 0.099 is below 0.100 is arithmetic. Whether the reading, together with other information, supports the particular false-start finding is a question of application. Where the threshold should sit is a question of rule design. en.before: This transformation calls for caution, because it alters the relationship between measurement and the measured. Ideally, measurement is passive: it records something that has happened without intervening in it. A ruler measuring a length does not change that length. The 0.100-second line is different. Once backed by disqualification, it ceases to be a passive record and actively shapes the behaviour it measures. Athletes know the line is there and adjust themselves to it. Measurement becomes intervention; the ruler begins changing what it measures. Once that happens, the resulting number is no longer purely an expression of human ability. It combines actual ability with people's avoidance of the line. Increasingly slow reaction times measured by the construct do not necessarily mean that people are reacting more slowly. More likely, people are deliberately yielding for safety.
en.after: This brings the relationship between measurement and the measured into view. A ruler may simply record an existing length; a rule backed by disqualification may prompt adjustment in advance. Recorded reaction times can therefore reflect both bodily capacity and avoidance of risk. Slower averages across rule regimes are consistent with that strategic explanation, but do not alone prove deliberate slowing by every athlete or exclude changes in equipment, fields and conditions. The question is how ability and institutional conditions jointly shape the numbers.

en.before: It is worth placing this question of the power of closure briefly within an earlier history, because two different roles of closure were already at issue when finish photography appeared. At Los Angeles in 1932 there were two cases of opposite character that must be kept separate. In the men's 100 metres, Tolan and Metcalfe both received official times of 10.3 seconds. The finish was extremely close, and officials carefully examined the photographic record. The official result was never changed to a tie: Tolan was first. A later claim often says that Metcalfe would have won under today's rules. That is a historically grounded counterfactual, because the old standard then required the whole body to pass completely beyond the finish line, and Tolan fulfilled that standard earlier. But the counterfactual cannot be merged with the actual ruling. The stronger claim that the photography proved Metcalfe had won and the officials deliberately awarded Tolan the title lacks reliable support. What can be established is the controversy, the difference in rules, and the final decision for Tolan. At the same Games, the men's 110-metre hurdles presented the opposite case. Keller was initially placed third; after film review, Finlay was awarded third place and the bronze medal. Here photography did not manufacture controversy. It supplied the evidence that closed it. From the start, then, the construct's interpretive tools operated in two directions. They could be accused of failing to close a dispute that should have been closed, and they could genuinely settle a placing misjudged by the human eye. Those must be distinguished, not lumped together as “controversial cases.”

en.before: This must be fixed firmly in place, because it dismantles a popular misunderstanding disguised as a technical limitation. People often assume that athletics results stop at hundredths because machines cannot measure accurately beyond them. The truth is the opposite. Machines have long measured more finely. The construct itself reads thousandths when needed to resolve qualification ties, and modern finish scanning has sampling intervals on the order of millionths of a second. Hundredth-of-a-second publication is therefore not a ceiling imposed by machinery. It is a representational format deliberately selected by the construct. The construct sees much more finely than it is willing to publish. Some of the precision it already possesses is retained internally and used only on specified occasions. This is a form of self-restraint on its own capacities. In that respect it resembles Tokyo's handing over of the switch: in both cases the construct possesses the ability to do something and chooses not to do it, or not to do it fully.
en.after: Two things need separating. Equipment can supply finer images than official results display, and rules use thousandths in certain qualification ties. But a scanning interval is not the accuracy of the entire measurement system: calibration, synchronization and interpretation still matter. Hundredths are therefore not simply the camera's ceiling, nor should every finer sample automatically become an official decimal place. Rules governing published times and placings decide which information has adjudicative force on which occasions. This has something in common with Tokyo: possessing more means of distinction does not mean always having to use them to the limit.

en.before: In the preceding sixteen essays, the construct consistently sought closure. It wanted to gather each matter into a determinate result: a name, a record, a placing, a victory or defeat. It repeatedly failed because something could not be gathered in, calculated, decided or accommodated. Those things it could not gather in were the remainders of the earlier essays.
en.after: Across the preceding sixteen essays, the construct repeatedly turned complex situations into names, records, placings and victories. Sometimes measurement and explanation remained apart; sometimes eligibility and definition left disputes; sometimes the institution chose not to make a certain judgment. What remained was not always a failure. It showed what a ledger could answer and what it left outside.

zh.before: 前面的余项，是构想闭合而闭合不了留下的。没进名单的名字，是构没接住的;算不清的成因，是构分不开的;不存在的身体，是构够不到的;被判为不可能的真实，是构用定义排除掉的。它们全都是构的能力的边界，是构想要而得不到的东西。
zh.after: 前面的余项有几种来路。名字可能被资格规则排除，成因可能没有被现存资料分开，身体分类可能安放不了连续的差异，起跑的读数也可能没有回答动作怎样开始。有些涉及能力的限制，有些涉及制度的选择，不能一概说成构想要却得不到的东西。这里换了一个角度：制度预先给当事人的共同选择，留出了位置。

en.before: Earlier remainders were what remained when the construct wanted closure and could not achieve it. Names absent from the list were what it failed to receive. Causes that could not be disentangled were what it failed to separate. Bodies that did not exist were beyond its reach. Realities declared impossible were excluded by its definitions. All marked the limits of its capacity: things it wanted but could not obtain.
en.after: Earlier remainders had different origins. Eligibility rules might exclude a name; surviving evidence might not separate causes; bodily categories might fail to accommodate continuous differences; a start reading might not explain how a movement began. Some involved limits of capacity, others institutional choices. They were not all things the construct wanted but could not obtain. Here the angle changes: the rules reserved a place in advance for the participants' joint choice.

zh.before: 这是余项这个概念的一次翻转。在前面十六篇里，余项一直是构的缺陷，是它力所不及的地方，是它想画那条线却画不准，或者画在了错误位置上的证据。而在这里，余项第一次不是缺陷，是设计。构没有被那个并列第一难住，它是主动地为那个并列第一，在规则里留了位置。它承认，有些时候，一个不闭合的结果，也可以是一个完整的，合法的，最终的输出。
zh.after: 这里可以看到余项的另一种样子。它不只是测量的不足或分类的困难，也可以是制度主动不再追求唯一赢家时，保留下来的空间。构没有被并列第一难住，而是事先为它留了合法位置。这个结果不再被收成一个人，却依然可以是完整、合法、最终的输出。

en.before: This reverses the concept of the remainder. In the preceding sixteen essays, the remainder was always a defect of the construct, a place beyond its power, evidence of a line it wanted to draw but could not draw accurately or drew in the wrong place. Here, for the first time, the remainder is not a defect but a design. The construct was not confounded by shared first place. It deliberately left room for it within the rules. It acknowledged that sometimes an unclosed result can still be a complete, lawful and final output.
en.after: Here a remainder takes another form. It need not be only a limit of measurement or a difficulty of classification; it can be space preserved when an institution deliberately stops pursuing a sole winner. The construct was not confounded by shared first place. It had reserved a lawful place for it. A result not reduced to one person can nevertheless be complete, lawful and final.

zh.before: 这个承认，比它看上去要重。这个系列从第一篇起，构的全部尊严几乎都建立在闭合上，建立在它能把一件悬着的事收成一个确定的答案的能力上。一个不能给出确定答案的构，看起来是失败的，无能的。所以承认一个不闭合的结果也可以是完整的，等于承认闭合不是唯一的成功形态，等于放下一部分构赖以立身的东西。而构能够做出这个承认，恰恰是因为它在别的地方已经足够强大。正因为它在绝大多数情况下都能闭合，它才承担得起在极少数情况下主动选择不闭合。一个软弱的，经常分不出胜负的构，是不敢立法允许并列的，因为那会暴露它的无能。只有一个强大到几乎总能闭合的构，才敢于在自己的规则里，为不闭合留一个体面的位置。
zh.after: 这个承认，比看上去更重。一个裁决制度很容易把唯一答案当作成功的标志，于是并列看起来像还没做完。东京却表明，成功也可以是承认既有比赛已经给出的平局，再让当事人共同决定不继续。我们不必由此推断只有强大的制度才敢这样做，也不必断定允许并列就是软弱。更重要的问题是：什么情况下继续区分有意义，什么情况下共同停止，同样可以成为制度认真对待的结果。

en.before: That acknowledgment carries more weight than it appears to. Since the first essay, almost all the construct's dignity has rested on closure, on its capacity to turn an unsettled matter into a definite answer. A construct that cannot supply a definite answer appears failed and incompetent. To acknowledge that an unclosed result may also be complete is therefore to acknowledge that closure is not the only form of success, and to relinquish part of what the construct has relied on to justify itself. It can make that acknowledgment precisely because it is already sufficiently strong elsewhere. Because it can close in the great majority of cases, it can afford to choose not to close in a very small minority. A weak construct that often cannot distinguish winner from loser would not dare legislate permission for ties, because doing so would expose its incompetence. Only a construct strong enough almost always to close dares reserve a dignified place for non-closure within its own rules.
en.after: That acknowledgment carries weight. An adjudicative institution can easily treat a single answer as the mark of success, making a tie look unfinished. Tokyo shows another possibility: recognize the tie already produced by the competition and let those concerned jointly decline to continue. We need not infer that only powerful institutions dare do this, or that permitting ties signals weakness. The more important question is when further distinction matters, and when stopping together can also be a result an institution takes seriously.

en.before: This forms an exact pair with Essay 16. There, the construct froze a physiological hypothesis into a definition and guarded the 0.100-second line so firmly that even evidence it had commissioned could not unsettle it. There, it gripped control of the final step tightly. Here, it holds the means of closure in the jump-off but deliberately hands over the switch that determines whether to complete that step. The same construct clings tightly at the start and releases its grip in the high jump.
en.after: This contrasts with Essay 16. There, research recommended lowering the start threshold while the rules retained 0.100 seconds; findings still had to travel into formal revision. Here, a path already written into the rules lets athletes tied for first jointly decide whether to enter a jump-off. One case asks how a standard is reconsidered; the other shows how an institution reserves a choice in advance. Both concern who decides the final step, but not a simple opposition between refusing evidence forever and relinquishing all control.

en.before: Holding on and letting go are not a contradiction. They are two ways the construct handles the final step. Some lines, it believes, must be drawn by itself and brook no intervention, even if the line's own footing is insecure. The 0.100-second threshold is one. Some outcomes, it believes, can be entrusted to those concerned to decide jointly, even though it is perfectly capable of deciding for them. Shared first place is one. The construct does not always want closure to the end. Sometimes it stops before the last step and leaves that step to those whom it judges.
en.after: Retention and delegation are different ways to handle the final step. Some standards need common application while remaining open to evidence and formal revision. Other outcomes already have an exit through which those concerned jointly decide whether to continue. The construct need not pursue a sole winner in every matter. It can also provide that an existing tie is a result, and that the next step is for the people it judges to decide together.

en.after: This differs from the direction emphasized in many earlier essays. Measurements, records, eligibility lines, scoring tables and starting thresholds turned unsettled matters into actionable decisions. Here a way to continue was also ready: the jump-off. Yet the rules left the choice of taking that next step to the athletes still tied for first, acting jointly.

en.before: In the championship race, there are usually no hired pacemakers. Athletes must consider position, qualification, fatigue accumulated through multiple rounds, the risk of being boxed in or impeded, and their opponents' abilities, while preserving reserves for the final sprint. World Athletics itself says plainly in describing championship 10,000-metre racing that these races use no pacemakers; athletes often conserve energy before settling the result over the final laps. The most rational strategy is frequently not to maximize average speed from the first lap, but to conserve energy and await a late acceleration.
en.after: In the championship race there are usually no hired pacemakers. Athletes consider position, opponents, the risk of being boxed in and reserves for a final sprint. Events with heats and semifinals add qualification and accumulated fatigue; the 10,000 metres at modern global championships is normally a straight final. World Athletics likewise describes championship 10,000-metre racing as often conserving energy before the closing laps. The best strategy is frequently not the highest possible average speed from the first lap, but finding the right moment to accelerate.

en.before: These are two systematically different kinds of race. Their objective functions differ: one minimizes time, the other defeats opponents. The assistance they permit differs; their optimal strategies differ. Physiological and competition data both confirm that they generate performances through different mechanisms.
en.after: These are two common, systematically different ways of organizing a race. One emphasizes time, the other defeating opponents; the pacing and information actually supplied may differ too. They can encourage different strategies without necessarily operating under opposite assistance rules. The distinction lies within one lawful event, and not every race falls neatly at either end.

en.before: A 10,000 metres is a 10,000 metres. The rules distinguish whether a race is legal, what assistance is permitted, and whether a performance can be recognized as a record. What they do not distinguish is the race's organizing purpose: pursuing a time or contesting a placing. In the published rules, no competition category called a “record race” stands alongside another called a “championship race.”
en.after: A 10,000 metres remains a 10,000 metres. Rules do distinguish World Championships, Olympic Games and other levels of competition, and regulate legality, assistance and record eligibility. But emphasizing a time in one race and a placing in another does not create two separate world-record events at the same distance. “Not naming” here means not establishing separate record categories, not never giving championships a name.

zh.before: 要先说清楚这个不命名的意思，因为它不是疏忽。一个构如果没注意到两种比赛的差别，那是它没看见，那不是这一篇要讲的。这一篇要讲的恰恰相反:这个构看得清清楚楚，它在自己的官方文字里，一遍又一遍地描述过这两种比赛怎么不同。它不是没看见，它是看见了，然后决定不在规则里把这个看见的东西，固定成两个名字。看见一个差异和命名一个差异，是两件事，而这个构停在了前一件和后一件之间。
zh.after: 这个不命名，需要说准。官方介绍已经承认两种比赛常有不同节奏和策略，所以不能简单说机构没有注意到差别。但这些描述也不能替代一份明确讨论过分设纪录类别、随后决定拒绝的会议记录。本篇能看到的是结果：差异被描述了，却没有因此成为两套纪录项目。看见差异，与赋予差异独立的法律类别，是两件事。

en.before: What “not naming” means must be clarified at the outset, because it is not an oversight. If a construct failed to notice the distinction between the two kinds of race, that would be a failure to see. That is not our subject. The opposite is: the construct sees perfectly clearly and repeatedly describes the difference in its own official writing. It has not failed to see; it has seen and then decided not to fix what it sees into two names in the rules. Seeing a difference and naming a difference are two things, and this construct stops between the first and the second.
en.after: “Not naming” needs precision. Official descriptions recognize different pacing and strategies, so the distinction is not simply unnoticed. Yet those descriptions do not establish a meeting at which separate record categories were considered and rejected. What this essay can observe is the outcome: the difference is described without thereby becoming two record events. Recognizing a difference and giving it a separate legal category are different acts.

zh.before: 这个设计很巧妙，而且它正是两个构能共用一张表的机关所在。设想另一种可能:如果规则把配速员定义成赛道外的辅助工具，那么有配速员的比赛，就成了一种被辅助的比赛，它的成绩理应和无辅助的比赛分开记。可规则没有这么定义。它把配速员放进了参赛者的名单，于是有配速员这件事，在法律上就不再是一种外部辅助，而是比赛内部的一种正常构成。一旦兔子是参赛者，雇兔子就和场上任何一个运动员领跑，挡风一样，是比赛内部的事，而不是从外面加进来的东西。这个身份的定义，一笔就把纪录赛和锦标赛之间那道本可以划出来的线，抹掉了。
zh.after: 这个身份安排，是共用纪录体系的一个重要条件。假如配速被列为禁止的外部帮助，相关成绩可能直接失去纪录资格；若另设辅助类别，才可能分开记账，两者都不是自动结果。现行规则把合规配速员放在参赛者中，同时限制套圈、轮换和场外介入。合法配速于是可以成为比赛内部的构成，而不是一出现就把赛事改成另一个纪录项目。

en.before: The design is ingenious, and it is precisely the mechanism that lets the two constructs share one table. Imagine an alternative: if the rules defined pacemakers as outside aids, a race with pacemakers would become an assisted race, and its results ought to be recorded separately from unassisted races. The rules do not define them that way. They place pacemakers on the list of competitors. Having a pacemaker therefore ceases, legally, to be external assistance and becomes a normal constituent of the race. Once the pacemaker is a competitor, hiring one becomes an internal matter, like any athlete on the track leading or sheltering another from the wind, rather than something added from outside. That definition of status erases, in a stroke, a line that could otherwise have been drawn between record races and championships.
en.after: That status is an important condition for a shared record system. If pacing were prohibited outside assistance, the performance might simply lose record eligibility. Separate accounting would require a further choice to create an assisted category; neither outcome is automatic. Existing rules place lawful pacemakers among competitors while restricting lapping, rotation and outside intervention. Legal pacing can thus be part of the race without automatically creating a different record event.

en.before: An honest gap must remain here. Recognition of the 1954 performance can be established; the full written reasons for its recognition are unavailable. It is reasonable to infer that the crucial difference between 1953 and 1954 was that in 1954 both helpers were participants in the same lawful race from the gun. But no meeting minutes have been found setting out the grounds for approval item by item. The outcome is established; the complete reasoning must not masquerade as established fact.
en.after: An honest gap remains. Recognition of the 1954 performance is established, but this essay has not obtained the complete written reasons. One observable difference is that 1954 did not repeat the 1953 arrangement in which Brasher let himself be lapped before taking up the pace. It is not that only the 1954 helpers started in the same race from the gun. That difference helps interpret the outcome without substituting for a recovered statement of the grounds.

en.before: A characteristic set of organizational modules can be identified in this record-oriented commercial racing. The target time is set in advance. One or more groups of pacemakers take successive portions of the pace. The principal athlete remains as long as possible in a sheltered position at a stable speed. Organizers select low altitude and a fast track or flat road course, choose a more suitable start time according to the weather forecast, and add time or record rewards to prizes for placings. Not every element appears in every race, but they recur in elite one-day meetings and fast marathons.
en.after: A characteristic set of organizational modules can be identified in this record-oriented commercial racing. The target time is set in advance. Pacemakers who start in the same race from the gun take successive portions of the pace. The principal athlete remains as long as possible in a sheltered position at a stable speed. Organizers select low altitude and a fast track or flat road course, choose a more suitable start time according to the weather forecast, and add time or record rewards to prizes for placings. Not every element appears in every race, but they recur in elite one-day meetings and fast marathons.

zh.before: 还有一个说法也要拆:节奏灯只能用于非锦标赛，绝不能出现在正式锦标赛。这个作为今天的规则命题，已经不成立了。早期的实务确实主要是在一日赛和纪录尝试里用，但2025年的欧洲室内锦标赛，已经正式部署了节奏灯。所以是否用于锦标赛，是一个赛事实施的选择和规则许可的范围问题，不是一个永久性的纪录赛专用的法律禁区。
zh.after: 还有一个说法要收紧：这种灯光设备永远不能出现在锦标赛。2025年欧洲室内锦标赛确实引入了Wavelight，但欧洲田径明确区分了用途：预赛使用部分赛段的参考灯，决赛在选手接近相关纪录节奏时显示纪录灯，并非照搬钻石联赛为运动员持续设定目标速度的直接配速。这说明设备可以进入锦标赛，却不能据此说两种比赛的灯光帮助完全相同。具体用途与赛事实施，仍然重要。

en.before: Another claim also needs dismantling: that pacing lights may be used only outside championships and can never appear in an official championship. As a statement of today's rules, that is no longer valid. Early practice did concentrate mainly on one-day meetings and record attempts, but the 2025 European Indoor Championships formally deployed pacing lights. Whether they are used at a championship is therefore a matter of event implementation and the scope of regulatory permission, not a permanent legal boundary reserving them for record races alone.
en.after: Another claim needs narrowing: that this lighting equipment can never appear at championships. The 2025 European Indoors did introduce Wavelight, but European Athletics distinguished its role: guide lights during part of the heats and record displays when finalists approached relevant record pace, not the Diamond League's direct aid continuously setting an athlete's target speed. Equipment can enter a championship without the assistance being identical. Its actual use and event implementation still matter.

zh.before: 这个争论，没有办法用一个实验来了结。没有可靠的实验能说，节奏灯固定贡献了多少秒。顶级的世界纪录，无法做随机的，盲法的技术对照，因为鞋，天气，配速员，运动员的状态，总是同时在变。所以这道光到底帮了多少，和前面几篇里那些无法归因的问题一样，算不清。
zh.after: 这个争论不能只靠一个实验了结：实验可以估计特定条件下节奏灯的影响，却不能独自决定什么帮助应当允许。至于某一次世界纪录，鞋、天气、配速、身体状态同时在场，不能把它重新跑成其他条件完全一样的对照。我们可以用研究和模型提出有条件的估计，不能从最终时间直接拆出灯光贡献了几秒。精确归因的困难，不等于这个问题原则上不能研究。

en.before: No single experiment can settle this dispute. No reliable experiment shows that pacing lights contribute a fixed number of seconds. Elite world records cannot be subjected to randomized, blinded technical comparisons, because shoes, weather, pacemakers and the athlete's condition are always changing together. Exactly how much the light helps is therefore impossible to disentangle, like the attribution problems in earlier essays.
en.after: No single experiment settles the whole dispute. Experiments can estimate the effect of pacing lights under specified conditions, but cannot alone decide what assistance should be allowed. A particular world record cannot be rerun with shoes, weather, pacing and bodily condition otherwise identical. Studies and models may yield conditional estimates; the finishing time alone cannot tell us how many seconds came from the lights. Difficulty in precise attribution is not impossibility in principle.

en.before: This is nearly an ideal natural comparison: the same person in the same year. In a record environment, 13:58; winning a championship, 14:54. A difference of 56 seconds. Those 56 seconds cannot all be attributed to form, because the competition's objective itself changes the optimal strategy.
en.after: The same athlete in the same year makes a vivid comparison: 13:58 in a record setting, 14:54 to win a championship, about 56 seconds apart. This reduces the temptation to attribute everything to different runners, but does not control weather, scheduling, form or opponents. Objectives and tactics belong in the explanation. Two times alone do not establish each factor's share of those 56 seconds.

zh.before: 女子一万米，切贝特又提供了一个更干净的同人对照。破纪录那场，比赛明确被设置为世界纪录尝试，用了目标节奏体系，成绩二十八分五十四;而2025年东京世锦赛，她本人夺冠的成绩是三十分三十七。同一个人，纪录环境二十八分五十四，锦标赛夺冠三十分三十七，差了一百零三秒。不能把这一百零三秒全归于状态，赛事目标改变了最优策略，这是核心的原因。
zh.after: 女子一万米又提供了同人的对照，但不是同一年。切贝特在2024年5月25日的尤金跑出二十八分五十四秒一四，那场比赛既以世界纪录为目标，也兼作肯尼亚奥运选拔。2025年东京世锦赛，她以三十分三十七秒六一夺冠，两次相差约一百零三秒。目标、配速和比赛展开值得比较，但还应同时记住年份、天气和身体状态的差别，不能把全部差额直接记在赛事结构名下。

en.before: In the women's 10,000 metres, Chebet supplies an even cleaner within-athlete comparison. The record race was explicitly arranged as a world-record attempt and used a target-pacing system, producing 28:54. At the 2025 Tokyo World Championships, she herself won in 30:37. The same athlete: 28:54 in the record environment, 30:37 to win the championship, a difference of 103 seconds. Those 103 seconds cannot all be attributed to form. The competition's objective changes the optimal strategy; that is the central reason.
en.after: The women's 10,000 metres supplies another within-athlete comparison, but not in the same year. Chebet ran 28:54.14 in Eugene on 25 May 2024, in a race designed as a record attempt that also served as Kenya's Olympic selection race. She won the 2025 Tokyo world title in 30:37.61, about 103 seconds slower. Objectives, pacing and the race's development deserve comparison, alongside differences in year, weather and form. The entire gap cannot simply be booked to competition structure.

en.before: All these differences are flattened by the uniform record table. Chebet's 28:54 and a hypothetical 10,000-metre performance in championship conditions enter the same table and occupy the same position in its logic. The table does not record the competitive structure in which the performance was achieved. It records only the time. At the level of the record table, the structure of competition, a variable that systematically affects performance, disappears.
en.after: Those differences do not create two record categories. Chebet's 28:54 and a legal championship 10,000 metres still enter the same event system. Official material can preserve dates, venues and meeting names through which context can be traced. The ranked time alone, however, does not unfold differences in pacing, tactics and objectives. Competition structure has not vanished from reality or the archives; it has not become the basis for separate accounting.

zh.before: 用切贝特这个同一个人的对照，是因为它排除了一个最容易的反驳。如果拿两个不同的人比，一个在纪录赛跑得快，一个在锦标赛跑得慢，总可以说是这两个人能力不同。可切贝特是同一个人，同一年，同样处在巅峰状态。二十八分五十四和三十分三十七之间那一百多秒，不可能来自能力的差别，因为是同一具身体。它也不可能全部来自状态，因为跨度太大。剩下的那个最主要的解释，就是赛事结构本身:一场为破纪录组织的比赛，和一场为夺冠进行的比赛，即便是同一个人来跑，也会跑出差着一百多秒的两个时间。而这两个时间，进的是同一张表。
zh.after: 用同一个人的成绩来比较，是为了少跨一道差异，而不是宣称其他差异都消失了。五千米两场在2025年，一万米纪录和东京夺冠则隔着2024与2025两个赛季。同一个人的能力与状态也会变，天气和对手更不会因为名字相同就固定。这样的对照不能给赛事结构单独估价，却提醒我们，时间差不能只用一个脱离比赛目的的“能力”概念解释。读懂数字，还要读它怎样被跑出来。

en.before: Using Chebet as a within-athlete comparison removes the easiest objection. Compare two different people, one fast in a record race and another slower in a championship, and one can always say their abilities differ. Chebet is the same person, in the same year, at the same peak of her career. The more than 100 seconds separating 28:54 and 30:37 cannot come from a difference in ability: it is the same body. Nor can the entire difference come from form, because the gap is too large. The chief remaining explanation is the competition's structure itself. A race organized to break a record and a race run to win a championship can produce times more than 100 seconds apart even when run by the same person. And those times enter the same table.
en.after: Comparing one athlete removes one layer of difference, not every other one. The 5,000-metre races occurred in 2025; the 10,000-metre record and Tokyo victory span the 2024 and 2025 seasons. The same person's ability and form can change, and neither weather nor opponents become fixed by the athlete's name. These comparisons cannot price competition structure independently. They do remind us not to explain times solely through an ability detached from the race's purpose. Understanding the number requires asking how it was run.

zh.before: 这个百分之三，不能单独证明锦标赛机制压制了世界纪录。因为还有别的混杂变量:气候，赛程的轮次，奖金，当年那个纪录本身的难度，训练水平，跑鞋，以及世界纪录本身已经越来越逼近生理上限。这些都会压低锦标赛决赛破纪录的概率，而它们和赛事结构无关。
zh.after: 这个约百分之三，不能单独证明某一种比赛机制压制了纪录。年代、天气、当时纪录的难度、训练和装备都会影响概率；轮次、激励与赛程本来也是赛事结构的一部分，不能又算作与结构无关的因素。这样的统计适合提示一个现象，若要估计原因，还需要比较口径一致的赛事，并处理这些共同变化的条件。

en.before: That three percent cannot by itself prove that championship mechanisms suppress world records. Other confounding variables exist: climate, the number of rounds, prize money, the difficulty of the standing record in a given year, training standards, running shoes, and the increasing proximity of world records themselves to physiological limits. These can all reduce the probability of records in championship finals independently of competition structure.
en.after: About three percent cannot by itself prove that a particular competition mechanism suppresses records. Era, weather, the standing record, training and equipment all affect probability. Rounds, incentives and scheduling are themselves parts of competition structure, not factors wholly unrelated to it. The statistic can identify a pattern; estimating causes requires comparable races and attention to these changing conditions.

Actual history is otherwise. Records are almost always broken in races organized specifically to break them, and almost never in championship finals. The two constructs bear the same name but touch their shared record line at very different frequencies.
en.after: What it directly tells us is that world records were rare in the championship finals within this stated scope. To say how much higher the per-race rate is in dedicated record attempts, we also need a definition and denominator for those attempts. This one proportion does not supply that comparison. Cases already illustrate differences in objectives and strategy. The historical count adds context without completing every causal or frequency comparison.

zh.before: 但要说清楚，用自行车来支持田径也应该分账，这是一个规范性的主张，不是一个历史的必然。自行车把两者分开，田径的传统恰恰是把两者结合在一个项目里。世界纪录，奥运冠军，战术能力，共同构成了田径这个项目一百多年的历史。如果正式地把账分开，反而会切断这一百多年的纪录连续性。所以田径不分账，不是它没想到，也不是它做不到，而是它选择了保留那个把两者合在一起的传统。
zh.after: 用自行车支持田径也应分账，是规范主张，不是历史必然。自行车把不同竞赛方式设为不同项目，田径则长期把世界纪录、奥运冠军和战术较量放在同一项目中。保留这种连续性，是维持合并的一种可理解理由，但本篇没有因此取得完整的制度动机。分组也不必抹掉旧纪录；怎样另设类别、保留既往成绩，仍有多种设计。

en.before: But one point must be clear. Using cycling to argue that athletics should also keep separate ledgers is a normative proposal, not a historical necessity. Cycling separated the two; athletics has traditionally combined them within one event. World records, Olympic championships and tactical skill together constitute more than a century of that event's history. Formal separation could sever that century-long record continuity. Athletics does not keep a combined ledger because it never thought of separating them or could not do so. It chooses to preserve the tradition that combines them.
en.after: Cycling can support a proposal for separate ledgers in athletics, not a historical necessity. Cycling defines different racing forms as separate events; athletics has long combined world records, Olympic titles and tactical contests within one event. Preserving that continuity is an intelligible reason for combination, not a complete institutional motive established here. Nor would new categories have to erase old records. Several designs could preserve past performances while adding classifications.

zh.before: 这个选择，放回这个系列里看，是有分量的。自行车证明了分账是可行的，一个体育项目完全可以承认，最快时间的能力和在对手互动中获胜的能力，是两种不同的技能，值得两个名字，两套账。田径没有走这条路。它把一百多年里的世界纪录，奥运冠军，战术较量，全都装进了同一个项目的历史里。这么做有一个真实的好处，就是纪录的连续性:从班尼斯特的三分五十九，到今天的每一个一千五百米成绩，是一条不断的线，可以一直比下去。如果分了账，这条线就会被切断，变成两条更短的线。所以田径保留合并，是用赛事结构这个变量的模糊，换来了纪录连续性这个东西。这是一个取舍，不是一个疏忽。
zh.after: 这个对照仍有分量。自行车说明，为不同竞赛方式分设项目是可行的；田径则保留了不同的组织传统。班尼斯特三分五十九秒四属于一英里的纪录史，不是今天一千五百米纪录的直接前一段，两者必须分清。在各自项目内部，旧成绩与今天的合法成绩继续比较，是合并制度的真实好处。是否值得进一步标注赛事结构，可以讨论，却不能只凭现状断言机构曾明确选择以模糊交换连续性。

en.before: Within this series, that choice carries weight. Cycling demonstrates that separate accounting is feasible. A sport can recognize that the ability to achieve the fastest time and the ability to win through interaction with opponents are different skills deserving two names and two ledgers. Athletics has not followed that path. It has placed more than a century of world records, Olympic champions and tactical contests inside the history of a single event. This has a real benefit: continuity of records. From Bannister's 3:59 to today's 1,500-metre performances, there is an unbroken line along which comparison can continue. Separate ledgers would cut that line into two shorter ones. Athletics preserves the merger by trading clarity about competition structure for continuity of records. It is a trade-off, not an oversight.
en.after: The contrast still matters. Cycling shows that separate events for different racing forms are feasible, while athletics retains a different organizational tradition. Bannister's 3:59.4 belongs to mile-record history, not directly to the 1,500-metre progression; the two must remain distinct. Within each event, continued comparison between old and new legal performances is a real benefit of combination. Whether competition structure deserves further annotation remains debatable. The present system alone does not establish an explicit institutional bargain trading clarity for continuity.

en.before: There are two constructs. A record construct: organizers can lawfully hire pacemakers participating in the same race, set target lap speeds, use approved pacing lights, select favourable tracks, weather and times of day, and link financial incentives directly to times or records. A championship construct: usually there are no hired pacemakers; athletes face qualifying rounds, direct opponents and the singularity of the title; the most rational strategy is often to conserve energy, change position and wait for a late acceleration.
en.after: There are two constructs. A record construct: organizers can lawfully hire pacemakers participating in the same race, set target lap speeds, use approved pacing lights, select favourable tracks, weather and times of day, and link financial incentives directly to times or records. A championship construct: usually there are no hired pacemakers; athletes face direct opponents and the goal of a title, with qualifying rounds added in events that have them; the most rational strategy is often to conserve energy, change position and wait for a late acceleration.

zh.before: 所以这个差异，成了一个余项。它真实地存在于每一场比赛里，它系统性地区分着一个二十八分五十四和一个三十分三十七，可是在那张统一的纪录表上，它不见了。表把两种不同的东西，当作对同一种能力的无条件测量，放进了同一个位置。那个被抹掉的，是生成这个成绩的赛事结构。
zh.after: 所以这个差异留在了数字之外。它参与塑造二十八分五十四和三十分三十七那样的比赛，却没有作为独立类别进入纪录排序。表能比较合法时间，但若读者把这个时间直接读成不受情境影响的能力，就会漏掉成绩的生成条件。问题不在表一定作出了这种宣称，而在一个清楚的数字，很容易被我们读成过于完整的答案。

en.before: The difference consequently becomes a remainder. It exists in every race and systematically distinguishes a 28:54 from a 30:37, yet vanishes from the uniform record table. The table takes two different things as unconditional measurements of the same ability and places them in the same position. What is erased is the competitive structure that produced the performance.
en.after: The difference therefore remains beyond the number. It helps shape races such as the 28:54 and the 30:37 without becoming an independent category in record ranking. The table can compare legal times. If we read a time as ability unaffected by context, however, we lose the conditions that produced it. The table need not explicitly claim that; a clear number can tempt us to treat it as too complete an answer.

en.before: This is another way for the construct to handle a difference. We have seen it unable to close a difference and seen it deliberately reserve space for non-closure. Here is a third way: it sees a difference fully, is fully able to name it, and chooses not to acknowledge it, letting two different things share one name and one table. Not an inability to separate, but a choice not to separate.
en.after: This is another way of handling difference. A construct may recognize and describe it without turning every difference into a separate event or record category. That need be neither denial nor the only reasonable design. We can still ask what one name and one table preserve, and what readers must recognize beyond the table.

zh.before: 而这个选择，落在一个三层的结构里，这个结构本身，才是这一篇最值得看的东西。第一层，规则拒绝命名这个差异，它不设立纪录赛和锦标赛两个类别。第二层，赛事组织却在持续地制造这个差异，一边是雇兔子，设灯光，挑天气的破纪录赛，一边是没有兔子，多轮赛制，比战术的锦标赛。第三层，纪录表再把两者重新合并，把两种结构里跑出的时间，放进同一张表，同一个进程。
zh.after: 这里更值得看的是三层关系。第一层，纪录资格没有按追时间与争名次分成两个项目。第二层，赛事组织让配速、信息、赛程与策略呈现不同组合，不是每场都一样。第三层，合法时间在同一项目里继续排序。这三层可以同时成立，却不能彼此替代：纪录分类不是比赛组织的全部，成绩排序也不是成绩来历的全部。

en.before: That choice sits within a three-layer structure, and the structure itself is what most deserves attention. At the first layer, the rules decline to name the difference: they establish no separate categories of record race and championship race. At the second, event organization continually produces the difference: on one side, record attempts with hired pacemakers, installed lights and selected weather; on the other, championships with no pacemakers, multiple rounds and tactical contests. At the third, the record table recombines them, placing times produced within both structures into the same table and progression.
en.after: The three layers are worth distinguishing. First, record eligibility does not split the event into time-seeking and placing-seeking categories. Second, organizers produce different combinations of pacing, information, scheduling and strategy; not every race is the same. Third, legal times remain ranked within one event. All three can hold without replacing one another. Record classification is not a complete description of organization, nor is ranking a complete account of how a result arose.

en.before: The rules decline to recognize it, events manufacture it, and the table merges it. The three layers operate simultaneously without pointing in the same direction. The rules say it is one event. Event organization says these are two kinds of race. The table says this is a sequence of comparable times. The construct has not resolved the contradiction among the three layers. It lets them coexist as they are.
en.after: Rules classify events, organizers produce particular conditions, and tables compare lawful times. There is tension between these layers, not necessarily a logical contradiction. The point worth retaining is that one measure can lawfully compare two performances without making all their conditions identical or ending judgment about ability and tactics.

en.before: This construct can hire someone to shelter you from the wind, install 400 lights to mark your pace, choose a cool evening and the fastest track, and write all this assistance into lawful rules so that your time enters the official records. In another race, it can remove all those aids and leave you to face opponents, fatigue and position alone. It knows perfectly clearly that these are two different kinds of race. Yet when it keeps the accounts, it writes the times produced by both on the same line. It has given the difference no name. The difference therefore remains quietly in every second that the table cannot explain.
